claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi alloy has a continuous dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The alloy exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking under room-temperature uniaxial tension.
The alloy has low ductility under room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Severe plastic deformation followed by controlled annealing will fragment the continuous lamellae.
The treatment will produce a patterned, equiaxed, or wavy microstructure.
The effective deformation-temperature window is 0.5–0.7 Tm.
A strain rate greater than 10^-1 s^-1 is required during deformation.
An applied pressure greater than 5 GPa is required during deformation.
Post-deformation annealing at 600–800°C for 1–10 hours will induce partial recrystallization and pattern formation.
Severe plastic deformation introduces high dislocation density and shear localization.
The deformation-induced dislocations and shear localization break the continuity of brittle lamellar interfaces.
Subsequent annealing reorganizes fragmented interfaces into a patterned configuration.
Patterned interfaces blunt crack tips.
The reorganized microstructure facilitates cross-slip.
High-angle grain boundaries and dislocation cell structures impede crack propagation.
Disrupting continuous interfacial stress-concentration pathways enables more uniform plastic flow.
The treatment will significantly increase ductility and fracture toughness.
The treatment will reduce catastrophic interfacial cracking.
The treatment will maintain or slightly improve yield strength relative to the as-cast lamellar state.
Conventional HIP at 100–200 MPa and 1000–1100°C will heal porosity while retaining the original lamellar structure.

contradictions.description: The experiment states that the HITM and conventional-HIP sets receive otherwise identical thermal cycles, but the specified HITM anneal is 600–800°C for 1–10 hours whereas the conventional HIP baseline is 1000–1100°C. The thermal histories therefore are not identical as written.
